title: Comprehensive Tangkhul Naga Grammar & Linguistic System
hindi_title: तंगखुल नागा विस्तृत व्याकरण एवं भाषा-विज्ञान निर्देशिका
author: Rev. William Pettigrew, S. Arokianathan & Tangkhul Language Scholars

sections.subtitle: Tangkhul Roman Alphabet & Vowel System
sections.content: Tangkhul utilizes a Latin-based phonetic alphabet introduced by Rev. William Pettigrew in 1897 and standardized by the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS). Vowels: a, ā, e, i, o, u (short and long variants).
rules: Long vowels marked with macrons (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū) distinguish lexical minimal pairs (e.g., 'ram' [country] vs 'rām' [dry field]).
Diphthongs include: ei (meira), ai (kakhai), ao (vanao), ui (ngashui), oi (choi).

sections.subtitle: Consonant Inventory
sections.content: Stops: p, t, k, ph, th, kh, b, d, g. Nasals: m, n, ng. Fricatives: s, sh, h, z. Liquids: r, l. Glides: w, y.
rules: Velar nasal 'ng' can occur in syllable initial, medial, and coda positions (e.g., ngalei [earth], thingrong [tree]).
Initial consonant clusters predominantly involve liquids: pr-, tr-, kr-, phr-, thr-, khr-.

sections.subtitle: Gender Classification
sections.content: Tangkhul distinguishes biological and social gender through suffixed markers.
rules: Human Masculine: -mayar / -va (e.g., ngalava -> youth/man, naomayar -> boy/son).
Human Feminine: -shanao / -la (e.g., shanaonao -> girl/daughter, ava -> mother).
Animal Gender: Male suffix -khon / -mayara (simuk-mayara [bull]), Female suffix -lui / -shanao (simuk-lui [cow]).

sections.subtitle: Number & Pluralization
sections.content: Plurality is marked by appending collective and pluralizing postpositions.
rules: Plural suffix -bing / -bina: mi (person) -> mibing (people), vanao (bird) -> vanaobing (birds).
Collective marker -saikora (all/entirety): ngalanaobing saikora (all the young maidens).

sections.subtitle: Core Case Postpositions
sections.content: Tangkhul is an agglutinative postpositional language. Cases are attached directly to the noun phrase head.
rules: Nominative / Agentive: -na (e.g., I-na shansera -> I have read).
Accusative / Dative: -li (e.g., Ali milu -> Give to him; Vanaoli thei -> Saw the bird).
Instrumental: -eina (e.g., Ngaphei-eina tulu -> Cut with a machete).
Genitive / Possessive: -wui (e.g., Shim-wui kuiphung -> The pillar of the house).
Locative: -li (e.g., Kaphung-li pamda -> Residing on the mountain).
Ablative: -wui eina / -li eina (e.g., Ukhrul-wui eina kazat -> Coming from Ukhrul).
Comitative / Associative: -le / -nga (e.g., Amei-le kazat -> Walking together with brother).

sections.subtitle: Personal Pronouns
sections.content: First, second, and third person pronouns with singular, dual, and plural distinctions.
rules: 1st Person Singular: I (I, me) | Plural: Ithum (we, us) | Dual: Inikha (the two of us).
2nd Person Singular: Na (you) | Plural: Nathum (you all) | Dual: Nanikha (the two of you).
3rd Person Singular: Ana (he/she/it) | Plural: Amathum (they, them).
Demonstratives: Hi (this), Chi (that), Hili (here), Chili (there).

sections.subtitle: Adjective Formation & Comparison
sections.content: Most Tangkhul adjectives are derived from stative verbal roots prefixed with ka- or kha-.
rules: Positive: kapha (good), kakhangar (heavy), kathuk (deep), kahung (red).
Comparative suffix: -shang / -meila (kapha-meila -> better than).
Superlative suffix: -saikora wui meila / -tak (kaphatak -> the very best).

sections.subtitle: Cardinal Numerals
sections.content: 1: akha, 2: khani, 3: kathum, 4: mati, 5: phanga, 6: taruk, 7: shini, 8: shet, 9: chiko, 10: thara, 20: maku, 100: sha akha.
rules: Numerals follow the noun they qualify: mi kathum (three persons), thingrong mati (four trees).

sections.subtitle: Tense and Aspect Suffixes
sections.content: Tangkhul verbs carry inflectional suffixes indicating tense, aspect, and completion.
rules: Root verbs take prefix ka- / kha- in citation/infinitive form: kasa (to do), kazat (to go), kapam (to sit).
Present Simple / Habitual: -i / -ya (e.g., I zat-ya -> I go).
Present Continuous: -da lei (e.g., I pam-da lei -> I am sitting / waiting).
Past Perfective: -ser-re / -haowa (e.g., Ana zat-haowa -> He has departed).
Future Tense: -ra (e.g., Ithum shok-ra -> We will come out / emerge).
Imperative: -lu (positive: Salu -> Do it!), -kha (negative: Masalu -> Don't do it!).

sections.subtitle: Negative Particles
sections.content: Negation in Tangkhul is achieved primarily through the circumfix ma-...-mana.
rules: Declarative Negation: ma- [verb root] -mana (e.g., I ma-thei-mana -> I do not see/know).
Stative Negation: ma-kalei (is not / does not exist) vs lei (exists).
Prohibitive Imperative: ma- [verb root] -alu (e.g., Ma-zat-alu -> Do not go!).

sections.subtitle: Interrogative Particles
rules: Polar (Yes/No) questions: -la? (e.g., Na pamra-la? -> Will you stay?).
Wh-Questions: Khi (what), Kachida (where), Khipa (who), Khitharan (when), Khipakha (why).

sections.subtitle: Basic Constituent Order (SOV)
sections.content: Tangkhul strictly adheres to Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) typology with head-final syntactic trees.
rules: Standard word order: Subject + Object + Verb (e.g., Mayarnao-na [S] kharai [O] phungda lei [V] -> The man is carrying the basket).
Modifier precedes or follows based on category: Demonstratives precede, numerals and adjectives follow head nouns.
Honorific and polite particles: -sho, -rei, -meo signify mutual respect between kin and elders.
